title: The name of the sword
hook: Tyag Mal, youngest son of Guru Hargobind, fights so bravely he is called Tegh Bahadur, brave of the sword

segments.voice: Yesterday, smallpox in Delhi, and the child Guru's last words: Baba Bakale. Your line was he served the sick. Did you reach the person you thought of? Day seventy-four.

Some people get their names twice. Once from their parents, and once from what they do. The kid everyone calls Doc because she bandaged the whole playground. The grandfather everyone calls Captain, though he never captained anything but the family. The second name tells you who a person became. The child Guru said the next Guru was at Bakala. To find out who he meant, we have to go back about thirty years, to Guru Hargobind's household, and to his youngest son, a quiet boy who got his second name on a battlefield. Today, a name that means a sword, given to a man who would then spend twenty years in quiet.
screen: `NAMED TWICE.` → `GURU HARGOBIND'S YOUNGEST SON.` → `A NAME FROM A BATTLEFIELD.`

segments.voice: He was born in Amritsar in 1621, and his parents named him Tyag Mal. Tyag means renunciation, letting go. Tradition remembers him as thoughtful, inward, drawn to quiet. Then came the battles of Guru Hargobind's later years, the ones from day sixty-eight. At the battle of Kartarpur, in 1635, the boy was about thirteen or fourteen. Tradition says he fought with such courage and skill with the sword that afterward his father gave him a new name: Tegh Bahadur. Tegh is a sword. Bahadur means brave. Brave of the sword. You might expect a boy with a name like that to become a great commander. He did the opposite. After his father's death, he went with his mother, Mata Nanaki, and his wife, Mata Gujri, to Bakala, a village near the Beas, where his mother's family lived. And there, for about twenty years, he lived very quietly. Tradition says he spent long hours in meditation in a small room below ground, working with his hands, keeping to himself, while the Guruship passed to his nephew, Har Rai, and then to the child Har Krishan. Brave, then quiet. People who met the grown man found someone gentle and still, who wrote hymns of calm detachment, some of which are now in the Guru Granth Sahib. The boy they called brave of the sword spent those years in stillness at Bakala, making no claim. Tomorrow, someone comes to the village looking for him.
screen: `TYAG MAL — LETTING GO.` · `KARTARPUR, 1635.` · `TEGH BAHADUR — BRAVE OF THE SWORD.` · `TWENTY QUIET YEARS AT BAKALA.` · then, large: `BRAVE, THEN QUIET.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: think where you were brave. Settle and breathe. Let one moment come back: a time you were more courageous than you expected. Maybe you spoke up. Maybe you stayed. Maybe you walked into a room you dreaded. It doesn't have to be dramatic. Feel it again in your body. Then notice how quiet that courage is now, sitting inside you, not needing to prove anything. Just rest with it. The bell holds the time.
Tegh Bahadur. Brave of the sword, the name given to the boy Tyag Mal after he fought bravely at the battle of Kartarpur in 1635.
Your line: brave, then quiet. Today, do one brave thing without announcing it, and let nobody know but you. Day seventy-four.

howItsDone: Sikhs remember Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, as both brave and deeply contemplative; his hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib, often about detachment and calm, are sung in gurdwaras and at Sikh funerals.

original.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi, from Persian: tegh, sword; bahadur, brave.

trapdoor: what you thought: a warrior's name.
what it means: a quiet boy called brave of the sword, who then spent twenty years in stillness.
what a scholar hears: tegh and bahadur are both Persian; his hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib were added later by Guru Gobind Singh.

notes: Editor review 2026-10-01: 'a man who would spend most of his life in silence' overstated (about twenty of fifty-odd years); fixed. 'It suited him' now tradition's memory. Replaced the closing uplift ('courage doesn't always keep shouting... the bravest people you know') with a concrete line pointing to tomorrow.
Birth 1621 in Amritsar; battle of Kartarpur 1635; age 'about thirteen or fourteen'. Confirm.
The underground meditation room (bhora) at Bakala is tradition; confirm.
'The Guruship passed to his nephew (Guru Har Rai, son of his brother Baba Gurditta) and then to Har Krishan (his grand-nephew)': confirm relationships.
His hymns were added to the scripture by Guru Gobind Singh (Damdama recension); stated in the trapdoor. Confirm.
howItsDone: sloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur are commonly recited at Sikh funerals (Bhog); confirm.
